question: What is the SolidWorks API, what underlying architecture does it rely on, and what languages are supported?
answer:
The SolidWorks API (Application Programming Interface) is a COM-based interface that exposes internal SolidWorks objects, methods, properties, and events to external software.

  • Core Architecture: Built on Microsoft's Component Object Model (COM) architecture. All SolidWorks objects inherit from COM dispatch interfaces.
  • Execution Model: Follows a Single-Threaded Apartment (STA) model, meaning all API calls that interact with the CAD session must run on the primary UI thread.
  • Supported Languages: C#, VB.NET, C++ (native COM/ATL), and VBA (Visual Basic for Applications). External scripts can also communicate via COM bridges using Python (via pywin32).

question: What is the difference between Early Binding and Late Binding in SolidWorks API automation?
answer:
Binding refers to how method calls and property access are mapped to the SolidWorks COM objects at compile time versus runtime.

FeatureEarly BindingLate Binding
Type ResolutionCompile time (requires direct reference to interop DLLs)Runtime (uses CreateObject / dynamic dispatch)
PerformanceFast: Direct vtable function callsSlower: Overhead of IDispatch::GetIDsOfNames and Invoke
IntelliSense & SafetyFull IntelliSense, strict type safety, compile-time error detectionNo IntelliSense, errors surface only at runtime
Version CompatibilityBound to referenced version; requires compatible interopsMore resilient to minor version shifts across installations

Recommendation: Always use Early Binding for enterprise add-ins and standalone automation tools written in C# or VB.NET.

question: What is the difference between a Standalone Executable (.exe) and an In-Process SolidWorks Add-in (.dll)?
answer:
SolidWorks customization typically falls into two deployment architectures:

  • In-Process Add-in (DLL): Runs inside the SLDWORKS.exe memory space. It implements ISwAddin, hooks directly into the CommandManager, registers custom menus/toolbars, responds instantly to document events, and offers maximum execution speed without inter-process IPC overhead.
  • Standalone Application (EXE): Runs as a distinct external Windows process. It attaches to or starts SolidWorks via COM (Activator.CreateInstance or Marshal.GetActiveObject). Useful for scheduled batch converters, ERP sync agents, and background queue workers.

Key Tradeoff: Standalone apps suffer slight IPC marshaling latency across COM boundaries, whereas Add-ins have zero IPC latency but can crash the entire CAD session if unhandled exceptions occur.

question: Explain the role of the ISwAddin interface and its mandatory lifecycle methods.
answer:
The ISwAddin interface (from SolidWorks.Interop.swpublished) is the core contract required by SolidWorks to recognize, load, and unload a .NET class library as an in-process Add-in.

It defines two required lifecycle methods:

  1. ConnectToSW(object ThisSW, int Cookie): Invoked when the add-in is loaded. Here, you cast ThisSW to ISldWorks, cache the session pointer and cookie ID, instantiate UI controls via ICommandManager, and attach document event listeners. Return true to signal successful initialization.
  2. DisconnectFromSW(): Invoked when the add-in is unloaded or SolidWorks closes. Here, you must tear down command tabs, remove UI toolbars, unhook all event handlers, and invoke Marshal.ReleaseComObject on COM instances to prevent dangling memory leaks.

question: How do you connect to an active SolidWorks session or launch a new instance using C#?
answer:
Depending on whether SolidWorks is currently running, you use either Marshal.GetActiveObject (or .NET Core/5+ equivalent) or Activator.CreateInstance.

// Connect to existing instance or create a new one
ISldWorks swApp;
try {
    swApp = (ISldWorks)Marshal.GetActiveObject("SldWorks.Application");
} catch (COMException) {
    Type swType = Type.GetTypeFromProgID("SldWorks.Application");
    swApp = (ISldWorks)Activator.CreateInstance(swType);
    swApp.Visible = true;
}

Important Note: In .NET Core / .NET 6+, Marshal.GetActiveObject was removed; developers must either pinvoke oleaut32.dll GetActiveObject via custom interop or use the Running Object Table (ROT).

question: Explain the SolidWorks Document Object Model hierarchy (ISldWorks, IModelDoc2, IPartDoc, etc.).
answer:
The SolidWorks object model follows a strict parent-child tree hierarchy:

  • ISldWorks: The root application object representing the running CAD session. Controls global settings, file opening/creation, licensing, and document collections.
  • IModelDoc2: The generic document interface inherited by all 3 document types. Contains shared logic like configurations, selection manager, custom properties, and rebuild actions.
  • IPartDoc, IAssemblyDoc, IDrawingDoc: Type-specific interfaces cast from IModelDoc2 based on IModelDoc2.GetType():
    • swDocPART (1) → cast to IPartDoc
    • swDocASSEMBLY (2) → cast to IAssemblyDoc
    • swDocDRAWING (3) → cast to IDrawingDoc

question: Why is COM reference counting critical in .NET SolidWorks development, and how do you handle Marshal.ReleaseComObject?
answer:
The .NET Common Language Runtime (CLR) wraps unmanaged COM pointers in Runtime Callable Wrappers (RCW). The .NET Garbage Collector is unaware of unmanaged COM memory pressure.

The Danger: If references to SolidWorks objects (e.g. IModelDoc2, ISelectionMgr, IFeature) are held by an RCW without explicit release, SolidWorks cannot unload files from memory, locks files on disk, or continues running in Task Manager as a ghost process after closing.

Best Practice:

  1. Explicitly call Marshal.ReleaseComObject(obj) or Marshal.FinalReleaseComObject(obj) in a finally block for long-running batch loops.
  2. Avoid the "two-dot rule" in COM calls (e.g., avoid swApp.ActiveDoc.SelectionManager.GetSelectedObject6(...) because the intermediate wrapper becomes orphaned). Assign each to an intermediate variable and release it.

question: How do you traverse features in a Part or Assembly document?
answer:
Feature traversal can be done using the linked list exposed by IModelDoc2 via IFeature.GetNextFeature() or using FeatureManager.GetFeatures().

Linked List Traversal Example:

IFeature swFeat = (IFeature)swModel.FirstFeature();
while (swFeat != null) {
    string featName = swFeat.Name;
    string featType = swFeat.GetTypeName2();
    
    // Traverse sub-features (e.g., sketch under an extrusion)
    IFeature swSubFeat = (IFeature)swFeat.GetFirstSubFeature();
    while (swSubFeat != null) {
        // Process sub-feature...
        swSubFeat = (IFeature)swSubFeat.GetNextSubFeature();
    }
    
    swFeat = (IFeature)swFeat.GetNextFeature();
}

Important: Always check for sub-features if you need access to underlying sketches, bend lines, or cosmetic threads.

question: What is the SelectionManager, and how do you extract selected objects and selection marks?
answer:
The ISelectionMgr interface accesses items currently selected by the user or programmatically in the active document.

  • Retrieval: ISelectionMgr swSelMgr = (ISelectionMgr)swModel.SelectionManager;
  • Count: int count = swSelMgr.GetSelectedObjectCount2(-1); (-1 checks all selection marks).
  • Object Extraction: object selObj = swSelMgr.GetSelectedObject6(index, mark);
  • Selection Type: swSelectType_e type = (swSelectType_e)swSelMgr.GetSelectedObjectType3(index, mark);

Selection Marks: Marks (integers: 0, 1, 2, 4...) allow grouping different inputs for complex commands. For instance, when creating a Loft feature, Profiles use Mark 1 while Guide Curves use Mark 2.

question: How do you read, write, and delete Custom Properties and Configuration-specific Properties?
answer:
SolidWorks uses the CustomPropertyManager interface to handle both file-level and configuration-level metadata.

// Accessing file-level vs config-level
CustomPropertyManager propMgr;
// For general/file-level:
propMgr = swModel.Extension.get_CustomPropertyManager("");
// For specific configuration:
propMgr = swModel.Extension.get_CustomPropertyManager("Default");

// 1. Add or Update Property
propMgr.Add3("PartNumber", (int)swCustomInfoType_e.swCustomInfoText, 
             "PN-90210", (int)swCustomPropertyAddOption_e.swCustomPropertyReplaceValue);

// 2. Read Property (Resolved vs Evaluated Expression)
string valOut, evalValOut;
bool wasResolved;
propMgr.Get6("Weight", false, out valOut, out evalValOut, out wasResolved, out _);
// evalValOut gives evaluated mass like '12.45 kg' when valOut is '"SW-Mass@Part1.SLDPRT"'

// 3. Delete Property
propMgr.Delete2("LegacyCode");

question: How do you traverse all components in an assembly recursively, and what is the difference between resolved and suppressed components?
answer:
In an assembly, the component tree is traversed starting from the root component via IConfiguration.GetRootComponent3().

public void TraverseComponent(IComponent2 comp) {
    object[] children = (object[])comp.GetChildren();
    if (children == null) return;
    
    foreach (IComponent2 child in children) {
        // Check suppression state
        swComponentSuppressionState_e state = (swComponentSuppressionState_e)child.GetSuppression2();
        if (state == swComponentSuppressionState_e.swComponentSuppressed) {
            continue; // Suppressed: geometry not loaded in memory
        }
        
        string compName = child.Name2;
        IModelDoc2 compModel = (IModelDoc2)child.GetModelDoc2(); // null if lightweight or not loaded!
        
        // Recursive step for sub-assemblies
        TraverseComponent(child);
    }
}

Important Difference:

  • Resolved: Model document and geometry are fully loaded into RAM. child.GetModelDoc2() returns a valid pointer.
  • Suppressed: Component is excluded from calculations and memory. child.GetModelDoc2() returns null.
  • Lightweight: Only graphics cache is loaded; must be resolved using child.SetSuppression2() before querying internal geometry.

question: What is MathTransform, and how do you transform coordinates between Component Space and Assembly Space?
answer:
Each component in an assembly has a Transformation Matrix (MathTransform) that defines its translation, rotation, and scaling relative to the top-level assembly origin.

  • Component Space: Local coordinate system where vertices, faces, and sketches are defined inside the part file.
  • Assembly Space: Global world coordinate system of the parent assembly.

Transforming Coordinates:

IMathTransform compXform = comp.Transform2;
IMathUtility mathUtil = (IMathUtility)swApp.GetMathUtility();

// Define point in part local coordinates (x, y, z)
double[] ptCoords = new double[] { 10.0 / 1000, 20.0 / 1000, 0 }; // in meters!
IMathPoint localPt = (IMathPoint)mathUtil.CreatePoint(ptCoords);

// Multiply point by transform to get Assembly World Position
IMathPoint worldPt = (IMathPoint)localPt.MultiplyTransform(compXform);
double[] worldCoords = (double[])worldPt.ArrayData;

To convert from Assembly space down to Component space, use compXform.Inverse().

question: How do you programmatically add assembly mates between two components using the API?
answer:
Assembly mates are created by pre-selecting the target geometric entities (faces, axes, or planes) with specific selection marks and calling IAssemblyDoc.AddMate5.

  1. Select Entity 1: modelDocExt.SelectByID2("Face1@Part1-1@Assem", "FACE", 0, 0, 0, true, 1, null, 0); (Mark = 1)
  2. Select Entity 2: modelDocExt.SelectByID2("Face2@Part2-1@Assem", "FACE", 0, 0, 0, true, 1, null, 0); (Mark = 1)
  3. Invoke AddMate5:
    swAssembly.AddMate5(
    (int)swMateType_e.swMateCOINCIDENT,          // Mate Type
    (int)swMateAlign_e.swMateAlignALIGNED,       // Alignment
    false,                                       // Flip
    0, 0, 0, 0, 0,                               // Distance / Angle params
    0, 0, 0,                                     // Tolerances
    false, false,                                // ForPositioningOnly, LockRotation
    0, out int mateError                         // Output error code
);

Always check mateError == (int)swAddMateError_e.swAddMateError_NoError to verify mate solver convergence.

question: How do you automate Drawing generation, view creation, and scale adjustments?
answer:
Automating drawing sheets involves IDrawingDoc methods:

  1. Create Drawing from Template: swApp.NewDocument(drawingTemplatePath, 0, 0, 0)
  2. Create Standard 3 Views: swDrawing.Create3rdAngleViews2(partFilePath) or custom model views: swDrawing.CreateDrawViewFromModelView3(partFilePath, "*Isometric", x, y, z)
  3. Adjust View Scale:
    IView swView = (IView)swDrawing.GetFirstView(); // Note: 1st view is always sheet background!
swView = (IView)swView.GetNextView();          // 2nd view is the first drawing view

swView.ScaleDecimal = 0.5; // Set 1:2 scale
swDrawing.ForceRebuild();
  4. Insert Projected View: Select parent view, then call swDrawing.CreateUnfoldedViewAt3(x, y, z, false).

question: How do you insert and export a Bill of Materials (BOM) table in a drawing or assembly?
answer:
SolidWorks allows inserting standard BOM tables using InsertBomTable3.

// In an active drawing view
IView swView = (IView)swDrawing.ActiveDrawingView;
string templatePath = @"C:\SolidWorks\templates\bom-standard.sldbomtbt";

IBomTableAnnotation bomAnn = swView.InsertBomTable3(
    false,                                           // Dock to anchor
    0.02, 0.02,                                      // X, Y positions (meters)
    (int)swBOMConfigurationAnchorType_e.swBOMConfigurationAnchor_TopLeft,
    (int)swBomType_e.swBomType_TopLevelOnly,         // Top-level, Parts only, Indented
    "Default",                                       // Configuration name
    templatePath,
    false
);

// Export BOM directly to CSV or Excel
ITableAnnotation tableAnn = (ITableAnnotation)bomAnn;
tableAnn.SaveAsText(@"C:\Output\AssemblyBOM.csv", ",");

question: What is the SolidWorks Document Manager (SwDocumentMgr) API, and when must you use it instead of the full SolidWorks API?
answer:
The SolidWorks Document Manager API is a standalone COM library (requiring a separate Dassault license key) that reads and writes file metadata without starting or needing SolidWorks installed on the host machine.

SolidWorks APIDocument Manager API
Requires full SolidWorks desktop license installedRequires lightweight DLL + Document Manager key
Spawns heavy CAD engine (high RAM & CPU footprint)Ultra-fast header parser (milliseconds per file)
Full access to 3D B-Rep geometry, sketches, rebuildingMetadata only: Custom properties, Configurations, BOM, Parasolid stream, XML, Cut lists
Desktop client automationServer-side indexing, ERP/PLM integrations, batch cloud extractors

question: How do you optimize execution speed during batch automation in SolidWorks?
answer:
Executing thousands of model updates can be throttled by graphics rendering, UI tree repainting, and disk I/O. Use these optimizations:

  1. Disable Graphics Rendering: Set swModel.Visible = false or open files silently with swOpenDocOptions_Silent.
  2. Freeze Feature Tree & UI:
    swModel.FeatureManager.EnableFeatureTree = false;
swApp.CommandInProgress = true;
swApp.EnableBackgroundProcessing = true;
  3. Suppress Dialogs: Set swApp.SetUserPreferenceToggle((int)swUserPreferenceToggle_e.swDisplayAllAnnotations, false).
  4. Open in Quick-View or LightWeight: For assemblies where only metadata or BOM is checked, load without full geometry.
  5. Batch File Closing: Always close documents without saving if read-only: swApp.CloseDoc(swModel.GetTitle()).

question: What is the B-Rep topology hierarchy in SolidWorks (Body, Face, Loop, Edge, Vertex)?
answer:
SolidWorks represents 3D solid and surface models using Boundary Representation (B-Rep), which separates topological connectivity from underlying geometry:

  • IBody2: Represents an individual continuous manifold solid, sheet body, or wire body.
  • IFace2: A bounded piece of surface (underlying geometry is ISurface: Cylindrical, Planar, Spline, etc.).
  • ILoop2: A connected boundary of edges defining outer or inner holes on a face.
  • IEdge2: An intersection between two faces (underlying geometry is ICurve: Line, Circle, B-Spline).
  • IVertex: A topological corner point (underlying geometry is IPoint).

Rule of Thumb: Topology links the entities together (e.g., face sharing edge), while Surface/Curve defines mathematical shapes.

question: How do you traverse all Faces and Edges of a Solid Body?
answer:
You retrieve bodies using IPartDoc.GetBodies2, then iterate through faces and edges.

IPartDoc swPart = (IPartDoc)swModel;
object[] bodies = (object[])swPart.GetBodies2((int)swBodyType_e.swSolidBody, true);

foreach (IBody2 body in bodies) {
    IFace2 face = (IFace2)body.GetFirstFace();
    while (face != null) {
        // Inspect underlying surface
        ISurface surface = (ISurface)face.GetSurface();
        bool isPlanar = surface.IsPlane();
        
        // Get Edges belonging to this face
        object[] edges = (object[])face.GetEdges();
        foreach (IEdge2 edge in edges) {
            ICurve curve = (ICurve)edge.GetCurve();
            double length = edge.GetLength();
        }
        
        face = (IFace2)face.GetNextFace();
    }
}

question: What is the difference between IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2 and selecting directly through entity pointers?
answer:
Both methods place items into the selection queue, but work very differently:

  • SelectByID2(name, type, x, y, z, append, mark, callout, options):
    • Identifies objects via string identifiers (e.g. "Top Plane", "Sketch1", "Face1@Part1-1@Assem") or spatial ray hits at coordinates (x, y, z).
    • Prone to broken references if user names change or feature tree renames occur.
    • Requires string parsing overhead.
  • Entity::Select4(append, data):
    • Directly called on the unmanaged COM pointer (IEntity, IFace2, IFeature).
    • 100% immune to rename bugs and coordinate rounding issues.
    • Significantly faster and more robust for programmatic loops and algorithmic operations.

question: How do you create and register a custom PropertyManager Page (PMP) in an Add-in?
answer:
A PropertyManager Page (PMP) embeds interactive UI inside the left panel of SolidWorks, standardizing user experience alongside native CAD commands.

  1. Implement IPropertyManagerPage2Handler9 in a listener class to handle button clicks, checkboxes, and slider changes.
  2. Call swApp.CreatePropertyManagerPage("Title", options, pmpHandler, out int errors) inside your add-in.
  3. Add controls using IPage.AddGroupBox, IGroup.AddControl2(id, (short)swPropertyManagerPageControlType_e.swControlType_XYZ, ...).
  4. Show page using pmpPage.Show() and destroy or hide with pmpPage.Close(true).

question: How does Event Handling work in the SolidWorks API, and what are common traps?
answer:
SolidWorks exposes events at the application level (DSldWorksEvents), document level (PartDocEvents, AssemblyDocEvents, DrawingDocEvents), and feature level.

Common Traps & Solutions:

  • Event Unhooking Memory Leaks: Every delegate attached (swModel.DestroyNotify += OnDestroy;) must be explicitly unhooked (swModel.DestroyNotify -= OnDestroy;) when documents close. Otherwise, delegates prevent garbage collection.
  • Re-entrant Event Loops: Modifying a model inside a ModifyNotify or RegenNotify event fires another regeneration, triggering an infinite recursive loop and crashing the process. Guard with a private bool _isUpdating re-entrancy flag.
  • Dynamic Document Attachment: When new files open, listen to swApp.FileOpenPostNotify to hook the new document's individual events.

question: What is a Macro Feature in SolidWorks, and when would you develop one?
answer:
A Macro Feature (IMacroFeatureData) is a custom, developer-defined parametric feature that lives directly in the SolidWorks FeatureManager design tree like any native Boss-Extrude or Fillet.

  • Core Callback Methods:
    • Regeneration Method: Executes when the model rebuilds. Generates custom B-Rep geometry and merges or cuts bodies using IBody2.Operations().
    • Edit Definition Method: Opens custom UI (PMP) when the user right-clicks "Edit Feature".
    • Security/Dimensions Method: Controls dimension display and handles parameter dragging.
  • Use Cases: Creating proprietary algorithmic geometry (e.g., custom gear generators, automated cooling ribs, custom perforations, dynamic lattice structures).

question: How do you read and modify Dimensions programmatically in SolidWorks?
answer:
Dimensions in SolidWorks are accessed via IDimension or IDisplayDimension.

// 1. Get dimension from Model Parameter Name
IDimension swDim = (IDimension)swModel.Parameter("D1@Sketch1");

// 2. Read System Value (Always in METERS / RADIANS regardless of document display units!)
double systemValue = swDim.SystemValue;

// 3. Modify Dimension Value in Active Configuration
// Set to 50 mm (converted to meters: 0.05 m)
swDim.SetSystemValue3(0.05, (int)swSetValueInConfiguration_e.swSetValue_InThisConfiguration, null);

// 4. Force Rebuild to update graphics
swModel.EditRebuild3();

Golden Rule: Always perform internal calculations in SI Units (Meters, Radians, Kilograms, Seconds). SystemValue ignores inch/millimeter document settings.

question: How do you automate Sheet Metal operations (Flat Pattern, Bends, Cut Lists)?
answer:
Sheet metal parts contain specialized features and folder collections:

  • Unfolding / Flat Pattern: Find the FlatPattern feature in the tree. To unsuppress: swFeat.SetSuppression2((int)swFeatureSuppressionAction_e.swUnSuppressFeature, ...);
  • Export to DXF: Use IPartDoc.ExportToDWG2 with ExportOptions = 1 (export flat pattern geometry directly without creating a drawing sheet).
  • Cut List Automation: Traverse feature tree for CutListFolder sub-features. Access swCutListFeat.GetCustomPropertyManager() to read sheet thickness, bend allowance, blank size, and bounding box dimensions.

question: What is the SolidWorks PDM Professional (Enterprise PDM) API, and what key interfaces are used?
answer:
The SolidWorks PDM API (EdmLib) allows custom add-ins and standalone tasks to automate file vault workflows, card variables, check-ins, and version controls.

Key Interfaces:

  • IEdmVault5 / IEdmVault15: Entry point. Handles vault login (LoginAuto), database connections, and folder retrieval.
  • IEdmFile5: Represents vault files; handles LockFile (Check out), UnlockFile (Check in), GetFileCopy, and version retrieval.
  • IEdmFolder5: Represents vault directories.
  • IEdmEnumeratorVariable5: Reads and writes data card variables (e.g., Revision, Approver, ECO Number).
  • IEdmPos5: Linked list iterator for navigating tree structures and file history.

question: How do you automate checking out a file, updating a card variable, and checking it back in using PDM API?
answer:
A common PDM automation workflow implemented with EdmLib in C#:

IEdmVault5 vault = new EdmVault5();
vault.LoginAuto("EngineeringVault", 0);

IEdmFolder5 parentFolder;
IEdmFile5 file = vault.GetFileFromPath(@"C:\Vault\Part1.SLDPRT", out parentFolder);

// 1. Check out (Lock)
if (!file.IsLocked) {
    file.LockFile(parentFolder.ID, 0, (int)EdmLockFlag.EdmLock_Simple);
}

// 2. Update Card Variable
IEdmEnumeratorVariable5 varEnum = file.GetEnumeratorVariable();
varEnum.SetVar("ApprovedBy", "@", "AutoWorker"); // "@" represents file-level tab
varEnum.CloseFile(true); // Commit variables

// 3. Check in (Unlock)
file.UnlockFile(0, "Automated approval stamp via API");

question: How does Ray Intersection (IModelDoc2::RayIntersections) work, and what are its practical use cases?
answer:
IModelDoc2.RayIntersections fires a mathematical ray vector through the model from a specific origin and returns all solid bodies, faces, and coordinates where the ray hits.

// Parameters: Bodies array, Ray Origin (X,Y,Z), Ray Vector (dX,dY,dZ), options...
int hitCount = swModel.RayIntersections(
    bodiesToTest, originArray, directionArray,
    (int)swRayIntersectionOptions_e.swRayHitFace, 0.0001, 0.0001, out object hitFaces, out object hitPoints
);

Applications: Clearance checks, sensor line-of-sight validation, automated wall thickness estimation, and custom 3D point projection algorithms.

question: How do you handle configurations programmatically (adding, activating, suppressing features per config)?
answer:
Configurations are managed via IConfigurationManager and IConfiguration:

IConfigurationManager configMgr = swModel.ConfigurationManager;

// 1. Add new configuration
configMgr.AddConfiguration2(
    "Machined_Version", "Machined state comments", "Alternate part", 
    (int)swConfigurationOptions2_e.swConfigOption_DontActivate, "", "", true
);

// 2. Activate configuration
swModel.ShowConfiguration2("Machined_Version");

// 3. Set Feature Suppression in Specific Config
IFeature swFeat = (IFeature)swModel.FeatureByName("Fillet_Cast");
string[] targetConfigs = new string[] { "Machined_Version" };
swFeat.SetSuppression2(
    (int)swFeatureSuppressionAction_e.swSuppressFeature, 
    (int)swInConfigurationOpts_e.swSpecifyConfiguration, 
    targetConfigs
);

question: How do you export SolidWorks models to neutral formats like STEP, IGES, Parasolid, and 3D PDF?
answer:
SolidWorks uses IModelDocExtension.SaveAs3 or SaveAs with explicit export preferences.

IModelDocExtension modelExt = swModel.Extension;

// Configure STEP version export setting (e.g. AP214 or AP242)
swApp.SetUserPreferenceIntegerValue(
    (int)swUserPreferenceIntegerValue_e.swStepExportPreference, 
    (int)swStepExportPreference_e.swStepExportPreference_AP214
);

// Export to STEP file
int errors = 0, warnings = 0;
bool success = modelExt.SaveAs3(
    @"C:\Export\Bracket.STEP", 
    (int)swSaveAsVersion_e.swSaveAsCurrentVersion, 
    (int)swSaveAsOptions_e.swSaveAsOptions_Silent, 
    null, null, ref errors, ref warnings
);

Supported extensions are automatically determined by file extension: .x_t (Parasolid), .step, .igs, .pdf, .stl.

question: What is the difference between Pack and Go via API vs manual assembly file copy?
answer:
Manually copying assembly files using Windows Explorer breaks internal file paths, causing missing components and suppressed reference errors upon opening.

IPackAndGo handles this programmatically:

  • Extracts complete dependency trees including parts, sub-assemblies, drawings, design tables, and simulation results.
  • Enables programmatic prefixing/suffixing of all filenames (e.g., adding project codes).
  • Redirects all child references so the cloned assembly opens seamlessly.

Accessed via swModelDocExt.GetPackAndGo(), configured with output folders and file rename lists, and committed using swModelDocExt.SavePackAndGo(packAndGoObj).

question: How do you automate Sketch creation, constraints, and dimensions via API?
answer:
Sketches are created using ISketchManager:

ISketchManager skMgr = swModel.SketchManager;

// 1. Select Plane or Face
swModel.Extension.SelectByID2("Front Plane", "PLANE", 0, 0, 0, false, 0, null, 0);

// 2. Insert Sketch Mode
skMgr.InsertSketch(true);

// 3. Create Geometry (Units: Meters!)
ISketchSegment line = (ISketchSegment)skMgr.CreateLine(0, 0, 0, 0.1, 0, 0);
ISketchArc circle = (ISketchArc)skMgr.CreateCircleByRadius(0.1, 0, 0, 0.05);

// 4. Add Constraints (Geometric Relations)
swModel.ClearSelection2(true);
line.Select4(true, null);
swModel.Extension.SelectByID2("Point1@Origin", "EXTSKETCHPOINT", 0, 0, 0, true, 0, null, 0);
swModel.SketchAddConstraints("sgCOINCIDENT");

// 5. Exit Sketch
skMgr.InsertSketch(true);

question: What is the SolidWorks CommandManager, and how do you build custom tabs and icons in an Add-in?
answer:
The ICommandManager interface provides native UI integration in the SolidWorks ribbon toolbar:

  1. Call iCmdMgr.CreateCommandGroup2(groupID, groupTitle, toolTip, ...);
  2. Add toolbar command buttons with cmdGroup.AddCommandItem2("Button Title", index, "Tooltip", "Hint", imageIndex, callbackMethodName, enableMethodName, ...);
  3. Create a dedicated Ribbon Tab using iCmdMgr.AddCommandTab((int)swDocumentTypes_e.swDocPART, "MyTabTitle");
  4. Add command boxes to the tab corresponding to the group command IDs.
  5. Call cmdGroup.Activate() to register controls in the CAD session.

question: How do you detect and report interference between components in an assembly programmatically?
answer:
Interference detection is automated via IInterferenceDetectionMgr:

IAssemblyDoc swAssem = (IAssemblyDoc)swModel;
IInterferenceDetectionMgr intfMgr = swAssem.InterferenceDetectionManager;

// Configuration flags
intfMgr.TreatCoincidenceAsInterference = false;
intfMgr.MakeInterferingPartsTransparent = true;

// Calculate interferences
object[] intfs = (object[])intfMgr.GetInterferences();
if (intfs != null) {
    foreach (IInterference intf in intfs) {
        double volume = intf.Volume; // in cubic meters
        object[] compArray = (object[])intf.Components;
        // compArray contains the conflicting IComponent2 references
    }
}
intfMgr.Done(); // Cleanup solver buffers

question: How do you handle multi-body parts and distinguish between solid bodies and surface bodies?
answer:
Parts can contain multiple independent bodies (e.g. weldments, mold designs, split parts). You query bodies using IPartDoc.GetBodies2:

// swBodyType_e enum flags:
// swSolidBody = 0, swSheetBody (Surface) = 1, swWireBody = 2

object[] solidBodies = (object[])swPart.GetBodies2((int)swBodyType_e.swSolidBody, false);
object[] surfaceBodies = (object[])swPart.GetBodies2((int)swBodyType_e.swSheetBody, false);

foreach (IBody2 body in solidBodies) {
    string bodyName = body.Name;
    double[] massProps = (double[])body.GetMassProperties(0);
    double bodyVolume = massProps[3];
}

Multi-body boolean operations (union, subtract, intersect) are executed using IBody2.Operations2.

question: How do you perform Unit Conversion cleanly across the SolidWorks API?
answer:
The SolidWorks API strictly expects and returns values in MKS units (Meters, Kilograms, Seconds, Radians) across all internal methods, regardless of the UI settings (e.g., Inches, MMGS).

  • Length: 1 mm = 0.001 m | 1 inch = 0.0254 m
  • Angle: Radians = Degrees * (Math.PI / 180.0)
  • User Preference Units: Query active document display units using swModel.GetUserPreferenceDoubleValue((int)swUserPreferenceDoubleValue_e.swLengthUnitType) to format numbers back to user expectations when displaying UI dialogs.

Pro Tip: Centralize unit conversions into a dedicated static helper utility class (e.g. Units.ToMeters(double mm)) across your codebase.

question: How do you automate Weldment and Cut List properties generation in C#?
answer:
Weldment structural members generate a special Cut-List structure in the feature tree. To automate them:

  1. Traverse the feature tree and locate features with type CutListFolder.
  2. Cast feature to BodyFolder: IBodyFolder bodyFolder = (IBodyFolder)swFeat.GetSpecificFeature2();
  3. Call bodyFolder.UpdateCutList(); to guarantee bounding box and cut angles are recomputed.
  4. Query cut list metadata through swFeat.CustomPropertyManager to extract standard properties like "LENGTH", "ANGLE1", "ANGLE2", and "Total Weight".

question: What is the difference between IModelDoc2::Rebuild vs IModelDoc2::ForceRebuild3?
answer:
Rebuilding model geometry has different scope levels:

  • EditRebuild3(): Standard dirty rebuild. Only recalculates features that have been modified or marked as dirty in the current session. Fast, but may miss indirect dependencies in complex assembly contexts.
  • ForceRebuild3(bool topOnly): Ignores dirty flags and completely recalculates every feature in the design tree from top to bottom. Slower, but ensures 100% geometric integrity, updates mate matrices, and synchronizes cross-document equations.

question: How do you automate SolidWorks Task Scheduler to run batch scripts off-peak?
answer:
The SolidWorks Task Scheduler can be automated programmatically using the TaskScheduler64 type library:

  • Instantiate the scheduler service: ITaskScheduler app = new TaskScheduler();
  • Add tasks such as app.CreateTask(swTaskType_e.swTaskUpdateFiles) or custom executable scripts.
  • Configure target directories, recurse subfolders, file types (*.sldprt;*.sldasm), and start timestamps.
  • Run tasks automatically overnight to generate PDFs, rebuild drawings, or export STEP files without tying up engineer workstations during the day.

question: How do you create and manage Equations programmatically using IEquationMgr?
answer:
Global variables and mathematical equations are driven by the IEquationMgr:

IEquationMgr eqnMgr = swModel.GetEquationMgr();
int count = eqnMgr.GetCount();

// 1. Add global variable: "Width" = 150mm
eqnMgr.Add2(-1, "\"Width\" = 150mm", true);

// 2. Add relation: "D1@Sketch1" = "Width" * 2
eqnMgr.Add2(-1, "\"D1@Sketch1\" = \"Width\" * 2", true);

// 3. Re-evaluate equations
eqnMgr.EvaluateAll();
swModel.ForceRebuild3(false);

Pass -1 as index to append the equation to the end of the equation list.

question: Why should you never use multi-threading to call SolidWorks API methods directly from background threads?
answer:
SolidWorks is fundamentally a single-threaded COM application built on the Single-Threaded Apartment (STA) model.

  • The Risk: Calling any SolidWorks COM pointer from a background thread (e.g. Task.Run() or ThreadPool) causes deadlocks, memory access violations, RPC_E_WRONG_THREAD COM exceptions, or silent CAD crashes.
  • Proper Architecture:
    • Keep all SolidWorks API calls on the main STA thread.
    • Run heavy non-CAD workloads (database queries, network API requests, ERP lookups, JSON serialization) on background worker threads.
    • Marshal results back to the SolidWorks UI thread using SynchronizationContext, Dispatcher, or Windows Forms Invoke before making CAD API calls.

question: How do you automate Balloon placement and Bill of Materials linking in SolidWorks Drawings?
answer:
Balloons are inserted and bound to drawing views via IModelDocExtension.InsertBOMBalloon2 or AutoBalloon5.

IDrawingDoc swDrawing = (IDrawingDoc)swModel;
swDrawing.ActivateView("Drawing View1");

AutoBalloonOptions opts = swDrawing.CreateAutoBalloonOptions();
opts.Layout = (int)swBalloonLayoutType_e.swDetailingBalloonLayout_Square;
opts.Layername = "Balloons";
opts.Style = (int)swBalloonStyle_e.swBS_Circle;
opts.Size = (int)swBalloonFit_e.swBF_2Chars;

// Automatically generate balloons on all view components
swDrawing.AutoBalloon5(opts);

question: How do you register and deploy a SolidWorks C# Add-in on client machines?
answer:
SolidWorks discovers add-ins through specific Windows Registry keys and COM interop registration:

  1. Assembly Attributes: Decorate the ISwAddin implementation class with:
    [Guid("YOUR-GUID-HERE")]
[ComVisible(true)]
public class MyAddin : ISwAddin { ... }
  2. COM Registration: Run regasm /codebase MyAddin.dll to register COM vtables.
  3. SolidWorks Add-in Registry Keys: Add entries under:
    HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\SolidWorks\Addins\{YOUR-GUID} (or HKCU). Set Default = 1 (enabled) and Title / Description strings.
  4. Startup Flags: Add DWORD under AddInsStartup to control whether it loads automatically on boot.

question: How do you extract Mass Properties (Center of Mass, Moments of Inertia, Volume) via API?
answer:
Mass properties are queried using IModelDocExtension.CreateMassProperty:

IMassProperty massProp = swModel.Extension.CreateMassProperty();
// Set active coordinate system if needed:
// massProp.SetCoordinateSystem(swCoordSys);

double mass = massProp.Mass;                     // in kilograms
double volume = massProp.Volume;                 // in cubic meters
double surfaceArea = massProp.SurfaceArea;       // in square meters
double[] com = (double[])massProp.CenterOfMass; // [X, Y, Z] in meters
double[] moi = (double[])massProp.GetMomentOfInertia(
    (int)swMassPropertyMoment_e.swMassPropertyMomentAboutCenterOfMass
);

question: What is the difference between Silent Mode and UserControl when launching SolidWorks programmatically?
answer:
When launching SolidWorks from a background automation service:

  • swApp.UserControl = false;: Specifies that SolidWorks is controlled by an automated process. If the user closes the CAD window, SolidWorks will not terminate until the API releases the process. Prevents interactive prompts.
  • swOpenDocOptions_Silent: Passed to OpenDoc6 to suppress all missing font prompts, resolved reference warnings, and dialog boxes during file load.
  • Background Process Trap: If an exception terminates your external app without calling swApp.ExitApp() when UserControl = false, SLDWORKS.exe will remain trapped in Windows Task Manager consuming licenses and RAM.

question: How do you capture high-resolution preview images or thumbnails of models without opening them in the CAD GUI?
answer:
There are two primary methods:

  1. SolidWorks Document Manager API: Use ISwDMDocument13.GetPreviewBitmap() or GetPreviewBitmapBytes() to extract embedded PNG/BMP thumbnails directly from file headers in under 15 milliseconds.
  2. SolidWorks API (Offscreen): Open file silently in background: swApp.OpenDoc6(..., swOpenDocOptions_Silent, ...), hide graphics, and invoke swModel.SaveBMP(imagePath, widthInPixels, heightInPixels).

question: How do you automate replacing a component in an assembly with another part file?
answer:
Replacing assembly components programmatically is done via IAssemblyDoc.ReplaceComponents2:

IAssemblyDoc swAssem = (IAssemblyDoc)swModel;

// Select the component instance to replace
swModel.Extension.SelectByID2("MotorBracket-1@MainAssembly", "COMPONENT", 0, 0, 0, false, 0, null, 0);

// Replace with new component path
bool status = swAssem.ReplaceComponents2(
    @"C:\Parts\MotorBracket_HeavyDuty.SLDPRT", 
    "Default",                                   // Configuration name
    true,                                        // Match old mates where possible
    (int)swReplaceComponentsInstances_e.swReplaceComponents_Single,
    true
);

question: How do you debug an in-process SolidWorks Add-in using Visual Studio?
answer:
Because an add-in runs as an in-process DLL, you cannot launch it directly via F5 without binding to the host executable:

  1. Open Project Properties → Debug tab.
  2. Set Start External Program to C:\Program Files\SolidWorks Corp\SolidWorks\SLDWORKS.exe.
  3. Set Command line arguments (e.g. /r to bypass welcome screens).
  4. Set breakpoints in your C# code (e.g. inside ConnectToSW or button click handlers).
  5. Press F5: Visual Studio boots SolidWorks, attaches the CLR debugger, loads your add-in from its registered COM location, and hits breakpoints as you interact with the UI.

question: What are Third-Party Storage Stores in SolidWorks files, and how can custom data be saved inside models?
answer:
Enterprise add-ins often need to persist custom application state (e.g., ERP IDs, cost breakdown schemas, revision manifests) directly inside .SLDPRT / .SLDASM files.

SolidWorks offers Third-Party Storage via COM IStorage:

  • Access via IModelDoc2.Get3rdPartyStorageStore("MyAddinDataStore", true).
  • Allows writing raw binary streams, XML trees, or serialized JSON directly into OLE structured storage compartments inside the SolidWorks native file.
  • Data persists through Save/SaveAs operations and travels with the file, completely isolated from SolidWorks feature tree corruptions.

question: What design patterns and software architectural practices should be applied to large-scale SolidWorks Automation projects?
answer:
Enterprise SolidWorks customization requires resilient software architecture:

  1. Facade Pattern: Wrap raw COM interop calls inside high-level safe .NET wrappers (e.g., CADDocument, CADAssembly) to isolate COM marshaling and null checks away from business logic.
  2. Model-View-ViewModel (MVVM): Strictly decouple PropertyManager Page / WPF UI views from direct CAD operations. ViewModels hold state; Commands execute CAD tasks.
  3. Unit of Work & IDisposable: Implement IDisposable on wrapper classes to deterministically call Marshal.ReleaseComObject.
  4. Robust Logging & Telemetry: Log COM error codes (HRESULTs) to Serilog or NLog, since unhandled COM exceptions terminate SolidWorks abruptly.
